blocks.text: Managing your sales pipeline in Excel

Your sales pipeline needs to be clean and accurate. If your data is messy, your forecasting will be wrong. Start by using data validation to ensure your deal stages are consistent. Go to the Data tab and select Data Validation. This prevents you from typing 'Closed Won' in five different ways.
Essential Mac shortcuts for sales efficiency

These shortcuts are small but they add up. When you are moving hundreds of leads from a web export into your tracking sheet, these keys save seconds every time. Over a month, that is hours of your life back.

Excel often strips leading zeros from phone numbers or zip codes. This is a common frustration for sales reps. To fix this, change the cell format to Text before you paste your data. Right click the cell, choose Format Cells, and select Text. This ensures your data remains exactly as you entered it.
Automating your reporting with pivot tables

You do not need to manually sum your sales totals every Monday. A pivot table does this in seconds. Select your data range, go to Insert, and click PivotTable. Drag your Sales Rep field to Rows and your Deal Value to Values. You now have a live view of your team performance.
Handling large datasets on your Mac

Excel on Mac handles over one million rows, but performance can drop if your sheet is too complex. Avoid using too many volatile formulas like OFFSET or INDIRECT. If your sheet feels slow, try to copy your data and paste it as values to break the calculation chains.

Use conditional formatting to spot duplicates in your lead list. Select your email column, go to Home > Conditional Formatting > Highlight Cells Rules > Duplicate Values. This is a quick way to ensure you are not calling the same prospect twice.

faq.question: Does Excel on Mac support all Windows features?
faq.answer: Most features are identical, but some advanced tools like Power Pivot are not available on the Mac version. You can still perform most sales tasks efficiently.

faq.question: How do I speed up Excel when it gets slow?
faq.answer: Reduce the number of complex formulas, remove unused formatting, and consider converting static data ranges into tables using Command + T.
